The psalm calls the LORD a refuge for the oppressed, but does not say all the oppressed know where to go.
Not answering a cry is not necessarily the opposite of not ignoring it. The verse does not say every cry is answered.
The verse gives David's purpose, but does not say praise will be the first thing he does.
The verse does not say David wants to be where the people are or that he is going to the gates.
The psalm does not mention big armies. The explanation adds them to its picture of the nations.
The verse does not say the needy have the least ability to defend themselves or give that as the reason for the psalmist's cry.

The verse does not say things go badly for the wicked man or describe what he does when they do.
The verse says there is no God in his schemes; it does not say what he does on holy days.
The verse does not say whether the wicked man is thinking about forgiveness.
The wicked man's claim that God does not see does not establish that he thinks God is not on any side.
The verse calls God the helper of the fatherless; it does not say they have nobody else to stand up for them.
The verse does not say the powerful already have plenty of help.
The psalm does not say the wicked man used his arm against the helpless.
